proposed_repo_changes: route Telegram ingress through a canonical assistant turn orchestrator
server-bind Telegram identities and scope grants
add a compiled capability manifest covering typed actions, UI actions, routes, queries, and external tools
add a normalized question read model and list_questions tool
add durable scoped memory/preference records and lifecycle events
add safe web search and connector policy adapters
add restart-safe ingress/outbox processing and worker heartbeats
remove or disable legacy webhook and direct Telegram bypasses after shadow parity
add generated parity, language, scope, no-write, approval, reliability, and live-smoke tests
tests_expected: node --check for every changed JavaScript/MJS file
focused sidekick-v2 unit and integration tests
separately approved hosted smoke for Shloimie and Rabbi
known_blockers: Current master and live worker versions must be refreshed at pickup.
Production migration/deployment/live messaging require separate approval.
Some UI actions need an explicit assistant mapping or intentional exclusion decision.
risk_notes: server.js is a high-collision file and must not be edited in parallel lanes
super-admin authority must never be inferred from a Telegram request body
private data must be filtered before model or web-search egress
memory sharing means policy-controlled namespaces, never a global transcript pool
legacy Telegram direct commands must not survive as hidden approval bypasses
handoff_rules: Audit current repo and local dirty state before applying.
Execute the prepared lanes in dependency order; do not solve the whole system in one unreviewable patch.
Use additive idempotent migrations and preserve compatibility until shadow parity passes.
Do not perform external effects without exact operator approval.
Do not mark Done without pushed code, correct deployment, runtime version proof, and approved live smoke for server-visible behavior.
